commonErrors: Scoring the lateral ventricles together instead of separately.
Mixing Graeb and modified Graeb scores.
name: Graeb Score

version.label: Original Graeb score (Graeb et al. 1982)
version.detail: Each lateral ventricle 0–4; third and fourth ventricles 0–2 each; total 0–12. The modified Graeb score (Morgan 2013, 0–32) is a different instrument.

purpose: Semi-quantitative CT grading of intraventricular haemorrhage burden.
intendedPopulation: Patients with intraventricular haemorrhage on CT (primary or secondary to ICH or SAH).

resultStates.label: No intraventricular blood
resultStates.summary: No intraventricular blood on this scan at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Small amounts of blood can be missed; scan timing matters.

resultStates.label: Graeb {total}
resultStates.summary: Higher scores indicate more intraventricular blood and ventricular expansion.
resultStates.detail: Interpret with clinical status, hydrocephalus and serial imaging.

clinicalContext.text: A long-standing semi-quantitative IVH grade, used in studies of IVH and its treatment.

clinicalInsights.text: Ventricular expansion is recorded; correlate with clinical signs of hydrocephalus.
The modified Graeb score scores more regions and correlated better with IVH volume in its derivation study.

limitations.text: Coarse categories correlate only moderately with measured IVH volume.

limitations: Does not include parenchymal haematoma or subarachnoid blood.

confounders.effect: Blood redistributes and clears over time.
Alters ventricular size and blood distribution.

guideSections.what: A 0–12 CT grade of intraventricular blood across the lateral, third and fourth ventricles.
guideSections.whenToUse: Describing IVH burden on CT, including serial scans.
guideSections.howToPerform: Score each lateral ventricle separately from 0 to 4. Score the third and fourth ventricles from 0 to 2. Add the four scores.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A descriptor of IVH burden used alongside clinical assessment and other imaging findings.

sources.citation: Graeb DA, Robertson WD, Lapointe JS, Nugent RA, Harrison PB. Computed tomographic diagnosis of intraventricular hemorrhage. Etiology and prognosis. Radiology. 1982;143(1):91-96.
